name: Qing dynasty

areaKm2.note: world_1880 polygon "Manchu Empire" = 11.01M km2 on the sphere; Qing claims incl. Mongolia, Tibet, Xinjiang and Taiwan ~11.4M km2.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1894 = 421,000k; HYDE/Gapminder (OWID) China 1894 = 384M (modern borders). Qing figures are uncertain.

activePersonnel.note: First Sino-Japanese War page, table of Qing army size by source (Olender 2014 p. 89): actual totals 375,000 (Gawlikowski) to 998,500-1,255,000; Olender 1,070,000-1,220,000; Green Standard 450,000-600,000 actual, Bannermen ~100,000 actual of 250,000. Japanese General Staff expected no more than 350,000 effectives. COW milper 1894 = 1,000,000.

trainedReserves.note: Provincial militia (tuanlian): Olender gives at most 300,000 (page table).

supportPersonnel.note: Artillery and fortress gunners ~30,000, navies ~15,000, arsenals and transport. Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess: the Qing state could not raise more than a few million men in total; effective modern forces stayed in the hundreds of thousands. audit 2026-10-30: kept at 0.006 (2.4M): the cited page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Sino-Japanese_War) gives 1.07-1.22M under arms plus at most 300,000 militia, so the ceiling is 1.6-2x the forces actually raised; no fetched source supports the 0.02-0.03 (8-12M) an era-median comparison suggests.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Braves (yongying) and trained units incl. the Huai Army (~45,000, the best armed, page) and Bannermen with modern rifles; page: 357,100 in Zhili, Shandong and Manchuria (Du Boulay) of which 125,030 trained men.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mixed Mausers, Remingtons, Winchesters and older muzzle-loaders

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: limited Western drill in the Huai Army only

count.note: Green Standard Army, a 600,000-strong gendarmerie-type force with no peacetime military training (page; actual 450,000-600,000).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: spears, matchlocks and some old rifles

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25. Evidence: no peacetime training (page)

count.note: Educated guess: Banner and Mongol cavalry with the field forces.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: traditional arms

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: horsemanship good, modern tactics absent

count.note: Educated guess: field guns, many Krupp, scattered among provincial armies; coastal fortress guns excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Krupp breech-loaders mixed with old pieces

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: ammunition mismatches, little practice

count.note: Paine, The Sino-Japanese War of 1894-1895 (2003) ch. 4: Beiyang Fleet 2 battleships (Dingyuan, Zhenyuan) and ~8 cruisers incl. 2 armoured, plus Nanyang, Fujian and Guangdong cruisers. Beiyang Fleet page: 78 ships of 83,900 tons in 1888, no new construction after 1888. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Dingyuan-class battleships unmatched in Asia but ageing, slow-firing guns

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: budget diverted to the Summer Palace 1889-94 (Beiyang Fleet page)

count.note: Torpedo boats, Rendel gunboats and training ships of the four fleets (Beiyang alone had 78 vessels of all types in 1888, page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: torpedo boats and gunboats

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: poorly maintained

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25. Evidence: Li Hongzhang's regional command, no general staff, armies uncoordinated

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25. Evidence: regional and personal armies, mass flight at Pyongyang

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.25-0.5. Evidence: unpaid, poorly led troops

weapons.note: Anchor: between 6 (1805) and 7 (1905). Evidence: imported magazine rifles and Krupp guns alongside traditional arms

ships.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: Dingyuan-class battleships of 1881-85

fortification.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: Krupp-armed forts at Port Arthur, Weihaiwei and Dagu

logistics.note: Anchor: 6 (magazines + requisition). Evidence: about 435 km of railway, Grand Canal, porters

communications.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: telegraph network since the 1880s

isr.note: Anchor: 6 (1805). Evidence: mistook Japanese scouting cruisers for the main fleet (First Sino-Japanese War page)

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: Qing revenue was ~3% of output and military and naval spending under half of it.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: handicrafts and a few arsenals and mills.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: dense peasant agriculture near subsistence.

annualCohort.note: Analogue: France 1805 snapshot ratio, males reaching military age = 0.95-1.15% of population per year (Elting ch. 9), applied to this population.

artillery.note: Educated guess: Jiangnan, Tianjin and Hanyang arsenal output of field guns per year.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: Fuzhou yard built only small cruisers; capital ships came from Europe.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: imperial post roads, mostly unimproved.

railKm.note: CHAT railline China 1894 = 435 km (Tianjin-Shanhaiguan and Kaiping lines).

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Tianjin/Dagu, Port Arthur, Weihaiwei, Shanghai, Fuzhou, Xiamen, Guangzhou, Ningbo.

merchantTonnage.note: Registered merchant tonnage 45k tons (China 1894, modern steamers only; the large junk fleet is unregistered and excluded, CHAT dataset https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta, variable shipton_all) x 1.5 (range 1.3-1.6). CHAT tonnage is registered (largely net) tons, so this may understate deadweight.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: porters and carts, rivers and canals.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses, mules, donkeys and draught oxen.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: depth, fortified ports and population; no harsh-climate factor against a neighbouring invader.

notes: Snapshot = Qing China in July 1894 at the outbreak of the First Sino-Japanese War. Territory and population = the Qing empire incl. Manchuria, Mongolia, Tibet, Xinjiang and Taiwan; Korea (tributary) excluded; includes is empty. Personnel: Bannermen, Green Standard, braves and trained units = active (Green Standard counted as infantry_light given its gendarmerie role); militia = trainedReserves. Army size is genuinely disputed (375,000 to over 1.2M, First Sino-Japanese War page table); the wide range is deliberate. Naval and artillery counts are reconstructions.
